headline: Microsoft rose 16.6% and added about $490B in market value — the largest one-day gain any stock has ever made.
quick: Microsoft's cloud growth sped up instead of slowing. The stock set an all-time record for value created in one session.
Meta spent almost everything it earned and fell about 9%. Same spending story, opposite verdict — the reason is the most useful thing on this page.
Apple and Amazon both report after the close tonight. Nothing is settled until then.
Timing note. This edition was written at 2:15pm in New York, with the market open. Prices below are live intraday, not the previous close plus premarket. They can still move before the 4pm bell.

macro.dt: The Fed held rates at 3.50–3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, with three officials dissenting in favour of a rise
macro.dd: Three regional presidents — Hammack, Kashkari and Logan — all wanted a quarter-point hike. That is the first three-way dissent in one direction since 2016. Rates staying high hurts fast-growing tech most. Their value sits in profits expected years out, and distant profits are worth less when money costs more.

macro.dt: Core PCE inflation has climbed from 3.0% in December to 3.4% in May
macro.dd: Core PCE is the measure the Fed actually steers by. Inflation drifting up rather than down removes the room to cut. That is normally a direct headwind to anything priced on far-off growth.

macro.dt: The gauge contradicts all of it
macro.dd: QQQ is up about 3.5%, on track for its best day since May 2025. Earnings are overriding macro today. But ten stocks account for 88% of that index move, from about a third of its weight. The rally is narrow, so it rests on a handful of results rather than broad demand — and the macro risk is still sitting there unpriced.

entries.happened: Azure grew faster than last quarter, and Microsoft raised next year's building budget by about a third.
figures: Azure     +43% vs 40% expected — up from 40% last quarter
Market value added ~$490B — a record for any stock
entries.why: The $678B of signed but undelivered work is the number that changes the argument. It means the spending is backed by orders already placed, not by hope. That turns capital expenditure from a cost investors fear into capacity they can count on. It also extends how many years of fast growth they are willing to assume — which lifts what they will pay per dollar of earnings, and moves the valuation more than the earnings beat itself.

foot.v: Yes. A 16.6% move and $490B added is a full repricing. Largely priced in, on live intraday prices.
Next quarter's Azure growth lands below the roughly 45% management guided.

entries.happened: Sales beat, profit missed badly, and spending consumed nearly all the cash the business produced.
figures: EPS       $6.18 vs $7.14 expected — and $7.14 a year ago
entries.why: Raising the floor of a spending range is a commitment. Raising the ceiling is only an option. Meta removed its own escape route. Free cash flow — the cash left after paying for buildings and equipment — is now close to nothing, so the buffer that funded buybacks and absorbed weak quarters has gone. Margins falling 12 points in a year shows the spend hitting profits now, while any payoff sits years away.

foot.v: Yes — the 9% fall reflects it. Largely priced in, on intraday prices.
Q3 shows margins stabilising and cash generation recovering.

note_after.title: The asymmetry worth understanding
note_after.body: Microsoft and Meta both raised spending sharply on the same night. One added $490B of value, the other lost about 9%. The difference is not the amount — it is what stands behind it. Microsoft can point to $678B of signed contracts. Meta cannot point to any. Investors call the first investment and the second cost. Ask that question of every capital-spending headline you read.

entries.happened: Intel announced nothing today. The move came entirely from the semiconductor sector.
figures: Results were 23 July, not today: revenue $16.1B (+25% y/y), EPS $0.42 vs $0.22 expected
Today's real drivers: Lam Research +20% — best day since 1999
Samsung: memory shortage worsens through 2027, lasts into 2028
entries.why: This distinction is the whole point. A sector move can reverse as fast as it arrived, because nothing changed at the company itself. Intel's own quarter was genuinely strong a week ago, but the foundry business still sells only about $293M to outside customers. Until that number grows, Intel's value rests on the same industry-wide demand that lifted it today — and that can be taken back just as quickly.

foot.v: A 12.5% one-day move with no company news. Read it as chip-sector beta, not as anything Intel did.
Memory and equipment demand cools, or a named 18A customer fails to appear.

entries.happened: Record quarterly revenue and a large profit beat, with crypto revenue still shrinking fast.
figures: Funded customers +7.2% y/y · operating margin 54.2% vs 44.4%
entries.why: Robinhood is swapping one volatile engine for another. Prediction markets growing tenfold more than covers the crypto decline, but both depend on trading appetite rather than on customers building balances. The real constraint is the 7.2% growth in funded accounts. Revenue per customer cannot rise forever, so slow customer growth eventually caps the whole model — and that is what sets the multiple investors pay.

foot.v: The 3.15% fall on Wednesday came before the results, not after. The actual reaction was −1.4% after hours, and the stock has recovered about 0.8% today. Three banks cut targets this morning, citing a July slowdown in new accounts. The market is pricing the account trend, not the quarter.

entries.happened: Apple reports fiscal Q3 results after the close tonight.
figures: Expected EPS     ~$1.88 vs $1.57 a year ago
entries.why: Nothing has happened yet — this is a scheduled event, not news. The one structural item: this is Tim Cook's last results call before John Ternus becomes CEO on 1 September. Succession and strategy comments therefore carry more weight than the quarter's numbers do.

entries.happened: Amazon reports Q2 results after the close tonight.
figures: Expected EPS     ~$1.82 vs $1.68 a year ago
AWS growth seen ~31%, up from 28% last quarter
Q1 free cash flow had already fallen 95% y/y to $1.2B
entries.why: Scheduled event. After today, the reaction will not turn on revenue. It will turn on whether Amazon can show contracted demand sitting behind its spending, the way Microsoft could and Meta could not. Its free cash flow line matters for the same reason — it is the test the market applied to both companies last night.

readthrough.title: Where Microsoft's spending lands
readthrough.body: A cloud company raising its building budget is not an isolated event — that money becomes revenue for the companies it buys from. Microsoft guiding to $255–260B is a direct positive for the chip suppliers (NVDA, MRVL, INTC) and for the smaller cloud builders chasing the same demand (NBIS). Together with Lam Research's results and Samsung's shortage warning, that is most of why chips rallied today on news that was technically about a software company.

note.title: Two clarifications
note.body: MRVL and NVDA both rose with the chip sector on no company news of their own — sector beta, not events. And NBIS is genuinely quiet: its $1B compute contract with Reflection AI was signed on 14 July, so it is not a story for today, whatever the stock does.
